Listen to others, even the dull and ignorant, because they also have their story.
entries.argued_against: dismissing people as dull or ignorant

entries.advice: Avoid loud and aggressive people, who are vexations to the spirit.
Do not compare yourself with others, which makes you vain or bitter.
Enjoy your achievements as well as your plans.
Stay interested in your own career, however humble, since it is a real possession.
Be cautious in business, because the world is full of trickery.
Do not let caution blind you to the virtue, ideals and heroism that also exist.
Be yourself, and especially do not fake affection.
Do not be cynical about love, which endures despite disenchantment.
Accept the counsel of the years kindly, gracefully giving up the things of youth.
Nurture strength of spirit to shield you in sudden misfortune.
Do not distress yourself with dark imaginings; many fears come from fatigue and loneliness.
entries.applies_to: times of fear, tiredness or loneliness

entries.advice: Beyond healthy discipline, be gentle with yourself.
Remember you are a child of the universe with a right to be here.
Trust that the universe is unfolding as it should, whether or not it is clear to you.
Be at peace with the deity, however you conceive of it.
Keep peace with your soul amid the noisy confusion of life and your own labors and hopes.
Be cheerful and strive to be happy, because despite its sham and drudgery it is still a beautiful world.
Recognize ego, an unhealthy belief in your own importance, as the enemy of learning, success and recovery.
entries.argued_against: a culture urging self-promotion and self-belief
entries.applies_to: people at every stage: aspiring, succeeding, failing

entries.advice: Talk less and work more; do not substitute talking about goals for pursuing them.
entries.argued_against: people who announce and boast instead of working

entries.advice: Choose to do meaningful work rather than to become someone important.
Always be a student: learn from someone better, peers, and someone you teach.
Replace fiery passion with sober purpose and realism.
Help those above you succeed and make others look good, clearing their path.
entries.argued_against: seeking credit early in a career
entries.applies_to: apprentices and those early in careers

entries.advice: Restrain yourself and endure slights and humiliations rather than reacting from ego.
Get out of your own head and see reality rather than a flattering inner story.
Do not let early praise or pride make you celebrate before the work is done.
Put in the long, unglamorous hours of work and practice.
After success, keep learning and do not believe your own legend or story of destiny.
Know what is important to you and pursue it, ignoring others' goals and refusing endless comparison.
entries.argued_against: envy and chasing more for its own sake

entries.advice: Avoid entitlement, the urge to control everything, and paranoia.
As your responsibilities grow, learn to manage and delegate instead of micromanaging.
entries.argued_against: leaders who cannot let go of control

entries.advice: Reflect on the immensity of the world and time to keep perspective on your smallness.
Stay sober and balanced, avoiding the intoxication of success.
Use setbacks as alive time to learn and act, not dead time spent waiting.
entries.applies_to: people in failure or difficult periods

entries.advice: Make doing your best work the goal and detach from recognition or outcome.
Judge yourself by your own internal standards rather than by external scorecards.
entries.argued_against: measuring worth by wins and applause

entries.advice: Own your failures and mistakes instead of defending yourself or blaming others.
Choose love over hatred and resentment toward those who wronged you.
Be humble, open to feedback, and willing to be a beginner.
Value sustained passion and perseverance toward long-term goals over raw talent.
entries.argued_against: the cultural bias toward natural talent
entries.applies_to: students, workers, athletes, anyone pursuing achievement

entries.advice: Remember effort counts twice: it builds skill and turns skill into achievement.
entries.argued_against: the belief that talent alone determines success

entries.advice: Develop interests over time by exploring, then deepening them, rather than waiting for passion to strike.
entries.argued_against: the idea that passion appears suddenly
entries.applies_to: people unsure of their passion, especially the young

entries.advice: Practice deliberately: set stretch goals, concentrate fully, seek immediate feedback, and refine.
Make practice a habit by doing it at the same time and place each day.
Connect your work to a purpose that benefits others.
Reshape your current job in small ways to align it with your values.
Cultivate hope by believing ability can grow and explaining setbacks as temporary and specific.
Organize goals under one top-level goal and drop lower goals that do not serve it.
Stay committed to your top goal but be flexible about the lower-level means to reach it.
Follow a family rule: everyone does a hard thing, picks it, and does not quit until a natural stopping point.
Parent in a way that is both warm and supportive and demanding.
Encourage children to stick with extracurricular activities for more than a year.
Surround yourself with a gritty culture, because groups shape individual perseverance.
Praise effort and learning rather than innate talent.
Value consistency over time more than short bursts of intensity.
Believe grit can grow; it tends to increase with age and experience.
Find role models whose work serves a purpose to inspire your own.
Understand that your mind is divided, a controlled rider on an automatic elephant, and train the elephant gradually.
entries.argued_against: the belief that reason simply controls behavior

entries.advice: Change your emotional style through meditation, cognitive therapy, and, where suitable, medication.
entries.applies_to: people prone to anxiety, depression or negativity

entries.advice: Challenge your distorted, negative thoughts as cognitive therapy teaches.
Look for your own faults and hypocrisy before judging others.
Use reciprocity to build relationships, while guarding against being manipulated by it.
Recognize happiness comes from between: getting relationships with others, work and something larger right.
entries.argued_against: the view that happiness comes only from within or only from without

entries.advice: Invest in close relationships and love, because strong social ties are vital to happiness.
entries.argued_against: the ancient ideal of detachment from attachments

entries.advice: Change the conditions of life you never adapt to, such as noise, long commutes, lack of control and shame.
entries.argued_against: assuming you will adapt to everything

entries.advice: Spend money on experiences and time with others rather than possessions and status goods.
entries.applies_to: people choosing how to spend money

entries.advice: Find work and activities that use your strengths and bring absorbed engagement.
Enjoy progress toward goals, since pleasure comes more from progress than from attainment.
entries.argued_against: expecting lasting joy from reaching goals

entries.advice: After adversity, seek meaning and growth, for example by writing about the experience.
entries.applies_to: people who have suffered loss or trauma

entries.advice: Cultivate virtue and character strengths as a source of happiness, not just rule-following.
entries.argued_against: modern ethics focused narrowly on rules and dilemmas

entries.advice: Seek elevation, awe and a sense of the sacred to lift you above the ordinary.
entries.argued_against: a flattened view of life without a spiritual dimension

entries.advice: Practice gratitude and acts of kindness to increase happiness.
Avoid relentless maximizing; settle for good enough in choices.
Balance competing perspectives and value insight from opposing moral and political views.
entries.applies_to: people in moral or political disagreements

entries.advice: Understand happiness depends on your set point, your conditions, and your voluntary activities.
